Hi! I'm interested in working on this issue to help migrate from `np.polyfit` to the newer `numpy.polynomial` API.

Before I start implementation, I wanted to verify:
1. Is this issue still relevant and open for contribution?
2. Are there any specific requirements beyond following the [numpy transition guide](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/routines.polynomials.html)?
3. Should I ensure backward compatibility or is a clean replacement preferred?

I'll wait for confirmation before starting. Thanks!

1. yes
2. no, just that tests pass
3. yes, i don't think there should be any breaking changes on the mitiq side.

PS i know you have a few other PRs open. I'd prefer to see those finished before this!

> Are there any specific requirements beyond following the [numpy transition guide](https://numpy.org/doc/stable/reference/routines.polynomials.html)?

You might want to read the earlier comments. Resolving this issue is not as straightforward as blindly applying the numpy transition guide. You will have to resolve the linked numpy issue first or follow Alessandro's suggestion in https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/mitiq/issues/2322#issuecomment-2098970442
A newer version of pennylane exists, but since this PR has been edited by someone other than Dependabot I haven't updated it. You'll get a PR for the updated version as normal once this PR is merged.

Hi, I'd like to work on this — can I be assigned?

I will let @natestemen decide on this. But to me this just looks like information & code lifted directly from the PT + ZNE tutorial (with some extensions to the code) and mostly LLM copy-paste of information.

Feel free to agree/disagree with the suggestion.  

I think it might be easier to use the [Qrisp -> Cirq conversion path](https://qrisp.eu/reference/Circuit%20Manipulation/generated/qrisp.QuantumCircuit.to_cirq.html#qrisp.QuantumCircuit.to_cirq) rather than Qrisp -> Qiskit -> Cirq path for `from_qrisp` in mitiq. 

The `to_qrisp` function in mitiq will still have to follow the approach taken in this PR though as `from_cirq` does not yet exist in Qrisp. It's one of my to-dos.
